key_insight: A Mamdani fuzzy-logic controller can continuously correct FSW tool tilt angle in response to torque, temperature, and plunge-depth deviation to help maintain weld quality.
engineering_relevance: This enables more adaptive and automatable tilt control for CNC-based friction stir welding, reducing defects caused by poor tool orientation.
method: Inputs: torque, temperature, and plunge-depth deviation.
Mamdani fuzzy inference with triangular membership functions.
Centroid defuzzification to compute tilt correction from an expert rule base.
evidence_signal: In MATLAB simulation, a sample input set (10 Nm, 45 °C, 0.5 mm deviation) produced a 0.224° tilt adjustment, with surface plots showing smooth response across a range of -0.4° to +0.5°.
watch_item: The approach is simulation-based, so real-world performance will depend on sensor noise, actuator response, and how well the fuzzy rules generalize across different FSW conditions.
paper_title: Advancing Tilt Angle Control in Friction Stir Welding using Fuzzy Logic
